clinician.trajectory_summary: A 59-year-old man with no significant medical history presented with a 5-day history of strong bitter taste in mouth, expressive aphasia, short-term memory deficits, confusion, occasional staring spells, and intermittent right hand spasms. Neurological examination confirmed expressive aphasia and short-term memory loss (unable to recall 3 items after 5 minutes) with otherwise unremarkable focal neurological findings. Imaging revealed a 4.0×2.3×1.5 cm partially calcified anterior mediastinal mass consistent with thymoma, along with bilateral subsegmental pulmonary emboli. Brain MRI demonstrated T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in the left frontal lobe, medial temporal lobe, and right cingulate gyrus (limbic system) with minimal enhancement, consistent with limbic encephalitis. EEG showed left frontotemporal periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges (PLEDs) with probable electrographic seizures. CSF analysis revealed elevated protein without pleocytosis and was negative for HSV 1&2, ruling out infectious encephalitis. Standard autoimmune encephalitis antibody panel (anti-NMDA, VGKC, LGI1, GABAB, GAD65, CASPR2, AMPA) was negative. The patient was treated with intravenous immunoglobulin G (2 g/kg over 3 days) and high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone (1000 mg for 5 days), with clinical improvement. He underwent successful video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery for tumor resection, with pathology confirming a type B2-B3 thymoma. Repeat brain MRI at 3 and 6 months post-treatment showed interval resolution of brain lesions, and neurological status returned to baseline with no further disease recurrence.

final.trajectory_summary: A 59-year-old man with no significant medical history presented with a 5-day history of strong bitter taste in mouth, expressive aphasia, short-term memory deficits, confusion, occasional staring spells, and intermittent right hand spasms. Neurological examination confirmed expressive aphasia and short-term memory loss (unable to recall 3 items after 5 minutes) with otherwise unremarkable focal neurological findings. Imaging revealed a 4.0×2.3×1.5 cm partially calcified anterior mediastinal mass consistent with thymoma, along with bilateral subsegmental pulmonary emboli. Brain MRI demonstrated T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in the left frontal lobe, medial temporal lobe, and right cingulate gyrus (limbic system) with minimal enhancement, consistent with limbic encephalitis. EEG showed left frontotemporal periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges (PLEDs) with probable electrographic seizures. CSF analysis revealed elevated protein without pleocytosis and was negative for HSV 1&2, ruling out infectious encephalitis. Standard autoimmune encephalitis antibody panel (anti-NMDA, VGKC, LGI1, GABAB, GAD65, CASPR2, AMPA) was negative. The patient was treated with intravenous immunoglobulin G (2 g/kg over 3 days) and high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone (1000 mg for 5 days), with clinical improvement. He underwent successful video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery for tumor resection, with pathology confirming a type B2-B3 thymoma. Repeat brain MRI at 3 and 6 months post-treatment showed interval resolution of brain lesions, and neurological status returned to baseline with no further disease recurrence.
